value.rationale: This is the complete real-and-complex Hilbert-distance classification for the natural infinite sequence of unit cycles, a canonical family in graph transportation geometry. Even real and all complex cycles attain the dimension-maximal Hilbert distance sqrt(n-1), whereas real odd cycles have the strict parity deficit (n-1)/sqrt(n). The scalar-field ratio sqrt(n/(n-1)) is a structural geometric distinction that neither numerical-index computations nor the existing single four-cycle distance expresses. The family/invariant is not an arbitrary finite slice and the all-dimensional bounds are sharp, though the proof uses an elementary invariant-ellipsoid method and the real vertex lemma is known.
